Higgsfield Videos

How we take a video that already works and make it hers, in her niche: Higgsfield for the girls and outfits, CapCut for the music and caption. Watch the Loom first, then follow this step by step.

Version v0.1Updated 10 Nov 2026Owner KTool Higgsfield · Factory · CapCut
Download PDF

01Watch first

Higgsfield video walkthrough, Kira (Loom by K). Watch all of it before you start. Come back to it any time.

Video not playing? Open it here: https://www.loom.com/share/1b2006235e404ee0bcfbbbdd1206b1b0

K makes one full video for Kira from start to finish. The steps below follow it, with the screenshots from it.

02What this is

We take a video that already did very well on social media (raw, made by a real creator) and remake it with her and her friends. Then three things turn it into a video for her niche:

The 3 things that make it hers1 · Outfits from her niche (Higgsfield).
2 · Music from her niche (CapCut).
3 · Caption: a winning caption, adapted (CapCut).

Keep what made the original good: the motion, the noise, the vibe, different girls in different outfits. Change only what makes it hers.

Two kinds: simple (this SOP, step by step) and complex (at the end).

03Before you start

  • Higgsfield open on the laptop, logged in. which account, how to log in
  • CapCut installed on the laptop.
  • The Factory open (Idea Bank, Song library, Reference library).
  • Your task: which video to copy, or "pick one from the Idea Bank".

04Step by step: a simple video

1

Pick the original

Your task gives you a video, or K or Leon sends one on Slack. If not: pick one from the Idea Bank, where we save videos that did very well.

Idea Bank: santor-media.up.railway.app/higgs · older ideas (about 3 months ago): santor-media.up.railway.app/prompts#ideas

2

Watch it, then download it

Watch it once and say why it works. In K’s example: several girls, sexy outfits, lots of noise, you feel you’re in the elevator with them. Then press Download (from Slack: download it the same way).

3

Higgsfield → Genjutsu

In Higgsfield: Video → Genjutsu. Check Motion transfer is selected. Clear anything left from before. Then press the empty box to add the reference video.

Why: Genjutsu takes a real video and puts our girls and outfits inside it. The motion stays the same.

4

Upload the original

Press Upload media, pick the video you downloaded, press Open.

5

Trim, then Confirm

Watch it once. Anything at the start or end you don’t want? Drag the yellow handles to cut it. Then Confirm. Click it in the library so it’s selected.

6

Count the girls, add her outfits

Count the girls in the video (K’s had 5). Press Add your characters and pick one outfit per girl: her, and her friends.

Keep what was good: the original had different outfits and different hair (brunette, blonde). Pick different ones too.

Don’t have her pictures? Factory → Add reference → Reference library → her niche (e.g. Star Trek): her outfits, her friends, her mum. Save the ones you need.

7

The prompt: 3 lines

AI is like a very smart child: it only does what you tell it. Paste this and change the numbers to how many girls you have:

copy motion and vibe from @Video1 but replace the characters in the video with my characters from @Image1 @Image2 @Image3 @Image4 @Image5 Keep the outfits from @Image1 @Image2 @Image3 @Image4 @Image5
  • Line 1 keeps the movement and the vibe. No dancing or jumping that wasn’t there.
  • Line 2 puts her and her friends in place of the girls. Image 1 replaces the first girl, image 2 the second, and so on.
  • Line 3 tells it to use the outfits too, not only the faces.
8

Check, then Generate

Model: Higgsfield Genjutsu. Quality: 720p quality rule (board says 420p). Double-check: the right video, the right outfits, the prompt. Press Generate. It takes a few minutes.

9

Watch it, then download

Watch the result all the way through.

  • Two girls swapped outfits? Fine.
  • Everyone in the same outfit, a face wrong, something AI-looking? Generate it again.

Good? Press Download.

10

Find her music

Factory → Song library → search her name (e.g. Kira) → find a song from her niche (K used the Star Trek Deep Space Nine theme) → Download.

A song you have in mind? Find it on YouTube. how to download it from YouTube

11

CapCut: video and music in

Open CapCut → Create project → Import → Downloads → the video, Import. Then the music, Import. Drag both down onto the timeline: video on top, music below.

12

Time the music to the hook

Play the video alone: where’s the hook, the moment you’d stop scrolling? (K’s: the doors open.) Bring the loudest, most recognisable part of the song in right there.

  • Cut the music where the video ends (the song is minutes long, the video is seconds).
  • Turn the video’s own sound down (K: about −10) so the music carries it, but the noise is still there.
  • Play them together. Adjust until it feels right.
13

The caption

Use a winning caption: words that already worked on a video like this one. Adapt it to her niche.

K’s example: POV: you’re the captain, and this is your crew ❤️. A Star Trek fan reads it and sees himself as the captain, in the elevator with them.

  • Text → Default text, then type it.
  • Font Rubik, Bold, small.
  • An emoji or two (e.g. a heart).
  • Place it where it doesn’t block a face. K put it in the middle.

where the winning captions are

14

Compare with the original

Watch the original, then yours. Same vibe, same hook, but now it’s hers and her niche: outfits, music, caption.

15

Export, save to Drive

Export from CapCut. export settings Save it in her Drive folder → Reels (SOP: Google Drive).

A 1:1 recreation task? Put the original and yours side by side in your task.

Copy the motion and vibe

Copy the exact motion

08Rules and nuances

everything not in the Loom: 420p, log-in, credits…

09Done means

  • The number of finished videos your task asks for.
  • Each one: her outfits, her niche music timed to the hook, a winning caption that blocks no face.
  • Looks real. Nothing AI-looking.
  • Saved in her Reels folder in Drive; original and yours side by side in your task.
  • Reviewed with K.

10Common mistakes

  • Everyone in the same outfit. Pick different ones.
  • Music that starts before the hook, or keeps playing after the video.
  • The caption over a face.
  • Changing what made the original good (the motion, the noise).

Added after every review with K
